verdict.rationale: Keycloak ships all the generic OAuth2/OIDC building blocks that a spec-compliant MCP authorization flow would need: discovery endpoints, dynamic client registration, client-credentials grants for service accounts, token introspection/revocation, and device-code grants (keycloak-docs-4, keycloak-docs-39, kc-supp-client-credentials, kc-supp-device-grant, keycloak-docs-52, keycloak-docs-53). But nothing in the evidence pack mentions MCP specifically — no guide, sample config, or community report of using Keycloak to front an MCP server with scoped tokens for remote agents. Missing for 10: explicit MCP integration documentation, resource-indicator/audience-restriction support tailored to MCP's spec, and any hands-on/community confirmation that an MCP server was actually secured this way.
